clue.text: Conceit shown by very naughty words professor rubbed out

indicators.note: something rubbed out is erased, so part of the words is taken away

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
naughty words are swearing, profane language
PROF is the short form of professor

explanation.surface: An arrogant professor whose swearing was struck from the record.
explanation.walkthrough: The professor's short title is struck out of the longer word, not out of the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit and vanity are synonyms, both meaning excessive pride in oneself.

clue.text: Detailed note brought up for minister?

blocks.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that minister is an example of a part of speech, not a politician or clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word minister, as in to minister to the sick, is an action word, a doing word in grammar.

clue.text: Angry scene with arsy drunk is unavoidable

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Each half has its own anagram signal and the two results sit side by side. Arsy is British slang for bad-tempered.

clue.text: Glorious day in August with Lloyd’s chiefs and the FT founders

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season. Lloyd's is the London insurance market.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth of August is nicknamed Glorious because it starts the grouse-shooting season in Britain.
